bank earnings persistence decreases with the increase of competition.

bank earnings adjustment speeds are faster in states where the interstate banking deregulation is implemented, and this effect is stronger for smaller banks and weaker for banks with more diversification, higher managerial efficiency, larger size, and higher safety.

the impact of competition and other bank characteristics on the persistence of bank earnings.
the effect of the deregulation and competition on bank earnings adjustment, and it is also related to the issue of the relationship between competition and the earnings quality of the U.S banks.
the impact of the deregulation of interstate banking on bank earnings persistence.

bank competition does not directly affect bank earnings persistence.
the impact of competition is to increase bank earnings adjustment speed, but the impact of competition can be weakened with the increase of a bank's abilities to maintain earnings.
the increase in competition has a positive effect on bank earnings adjustment, but the effect is mitigated by the ability to sustain earnings.

the competition in the banking sector is a double-edged sword: it can improve bank earnings adjustment speed but it also makes banks less capable of manipulating their earnings.
